title: eval_intent.yaml — the TYPED intent
description: The machine-readable half of skills/extract-eval-intent/references/eval_intent_schema.md, which is the prose owner. WHY IT IS TYPED: two intents authored from the same PRD, one night apart, carried 4 goals / 7 bare-label must_catch / 10 custom_metrics and 7 / 8 / 0 respectively, with 5 names in BOTH lists and only 6 policy names shared between the two eval sets that came out. The PRDs were the same size. That swing is one-shot authoring variance on an untyped document, and the gate downstream can only bound the damage — the schema is what makes the author consistent. The unit is the AXIS (one failure axis, one owner), each of whose failure modes must trace to a NAMED source, because the item that shipped flagged 'customer-supplied (not in inputs) — never verified' is the one that produced the census's stable contradicting pairs.

schema.description: Version tag. A document without it is a v1 intent (goals / must_catch / custom_metrics) and is READ, never mixed — see the migration note in the .md.

axes.description: One entry per FAILURE AXIS. The axis is the unit of the eval set: the recipe folds policies that share a guard, a scope and a surface, and coverage is credited by (policy, failure-mode) row — so an axis with three failure modes is one judge with three obligations, not three judges.

id.description: snake_case, UNIQUE across the document, so each axis has one name. The eval set's typed ledger (`out/obligations.yaml`) answers an axis by its position (`axes[i]`), not by this id.

axis.description: What a violation of this axis IS, in a few words — the same sentence that becomes the policy's `AXIS:` line. 'the agent should be helpful' is not an axis; 'a figure asserted without a tool result behind it' is.

failure_modes.description: The observable shapes this axis fails in. Each is a coverage row the ledger credits by obligation_id, which is what makes folding cost nothing.

id.description: snake_case, UNIQUE across the WHOLE document (not just within its axis). The night intent named five things in two different lists; one id space is what stops that.

describes.description: The concrete, observable failure shape — what a reader could point at in a transcript, a tool_events array or a world state. Abstract phrasing here is what produces a vacuous eval.

traced_to.description: REQUIRED, and the item this schema exists for. Every failure mode names where it came from; a mode nobody can trace is a mode nobody verified.

source.description: `customer` is legal and is the ONLY unverifiable one — it means the customer asked for this and no input document says it. It is declared, never disguised as a `prd` reference, because the backend's provenance tier decides on exactly this value.

ref.description: A NAME a reader can resolve: a PRD section heading, a scan finding id, a trace-brief section, a corpus doc id, or the customer's own question. Never a page number and never 'the PRD'.

quote.description: Verbatim from the source. REQUIRED for `prd` and `corpus` (a paraphrase of a term the judge grades is how one document comes to define 'resolved' differently from the other); optional elsewhere.

catcher.description: One of the canonical catcher tags when the shape matches an existing backend recipe — the backend lifts those verbatim. Omit rather than force-fit: a tag whose recipe grades a premise this suite never plants binds nothing.

surface.description: Where a violation of this axis is OBSERVABLE. Optional, but it is what lets the recipe fold two axes that share a guard and a scope, and what lets the co-binding bound count absolutes per reply surface.

notes.description: Anything the author wants the eval recipe to know that is not a failure mode.

preferences.description: Global authoring biases, unchanged from v1.
